description: TELEMETRY with ENCRYPTED set and CIPHER_ID = 1, so flags = 0x0006. payload_hex is a REAL ChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext and tag produced with the Python `cryptography` package, with key, nonce, AAD and plaintext published in the "aead" block below for reproduction. Together with aead_telemetry_gcm this proves CIPHER_ID actually selects the cipher on the wire rather than merely being carried.

frame.payload_hex: 9f 98 44 f4 4d dc 69 73 e1 7a c7 c9 90 fe c8 9d a8 34 f5 c8 7d 4e f4 26 79 3a 84 ae 3c eb fc be 95 2b ee 5c 97 ee c7 05 17 16 c5 b2 15 e3 e0 4a e4 d2 7e d8 66 95 da 2d 9f 98 a4 23

aead.cipher_id_note: Normative value of the CIPHER_ID sub-field (bits 2-3 of flags, mask 0x000C) for ChaCha20-Poly1305. It matches bits 2-3 of the flags value above.
aead.key_note: Fixed, public, sequential test key, documented only so this vector can be reproduced. NEVER use in production: a real key never travels on the wire and is never written down in the clear.
aead.nonce_construction: source_id || boot_id || sequence, each 4 octets little-endian (btp::aead_nonce). Derivable from the frame fields above; spelled out here only for convenience.
aead.aad_construction: The 36 octets btp::encode_header() writes for this header, with the version octet already 2 because ENCRYPTED is set. Derivable from the frame fields above; spelled out here only for convenience.
aead.plaintext_ascii: BTP v2 ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD test plaintext
aead.reproduction_note: payload_hex is the cipher's output over (nonce, plaintext, aad); the library appends the 16-octet tag, which is exactly the order the logical payload requires.
